prompts.task: Add OpenTelemetry instrumentation to the Express service in ./service. Assume no custom business spans are requested.
Instrument the Express service in ./service with OpenTelemetry while preserving the existing runtime and startup command. Add auto-instrumentation only; do not add custom business spans.

judge_inputs: Inspect ./service for resulting files when present.
Read ./last_message.md for the agent final response.
rubric: Configures NodeSDK with HTTP and Express auto-instrumentation.

Configures one version-compatible official console logging bridge with one batched OTLP log processor using @opentelemetry/exporter-logs-otlp-proto for the default http/protobuf path to the signal-specific local Splunk Observability Studio /v1/logs endpoint.

Exports the fixture's request-context warning as one record with its body, WARN severity, node-express-basic resource identity, and non-empty trace and span IDs while preserving console output without duplicate records.
Honors OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER=none and another explicit operator-owned exporter by installing no local log processor or console bridge while leaving the original console sink active.

Embeds the exact preflight-approved local receiver /v1/logs URL and enables the added log processor and bridge only when an explicit logs endpoint or generic-derived logs URL equals it; a log-only endpoint/header/protocol conflict or log exporter/processor/bridge construction failure emits a value-free diagnostic and skips the added log pipeline while traces, metrics, and the original console sink continue.

Keeps generic or signal-specific cloud endpoints, headers, credentials, and forwarding out of the application-log path; direct cloud remains trace/metric-only and logs stay local unless explicitly operator-owned.
Keeps service name and OTLP endpoint environment-driven.

Adds one graceful shutdown path that first stops intake, drains in-flight work, and emits final application logs, then flushes the SDK log processor together with the trace and metric providers exactly once; successful graceful completion exits 0 while drain/export failures and timeouts remain nonzero.
Does not rewrite the Express app structure unnecessarily.
